claim: The R-008 fire-signal family can distinguish exposed and occluded player-created fire signals while preserving production-owned hostile identity through approach, local behavior, departure, abstract return, camp interaction, and useful mixed outcomes.
material_proof: Bound family runs create a real brazier fire through ordinary player actions, receipt an exact two-tile retreat, and cite the smallest production events that identify signal channel, observer or responder, origin, dispatch or approach cause, bubble crossings, local policy, departure, durable return, and any save/reload boundary actually claimed. The indoor conclusion compares matched closed and exposed openings and separates light from smoke, sound, scent, pre-existing knowledge, and incidental contact. Camp conclusions separately cite locker, patrol, shakedown, and combat-escalation observations. Independent claims may have different verdicts in one run.

actor identity or simulation ownership is lost across a claimed bubble, save, reload, departure, or return boundary

already_accepted_evidence: Earlier roof-fire scenarios proved the generated flat roof, normal brazier deployment, charged-lighter ignition, SOURCE_FIREWOOD handling, and saved f_brazier/fd_fire result state; those setup primitives remain zero-credit context.

Focused camp tests already cover CAMP_LOCKER/CAMP_PATROL behavior and non-escalating shakedown watch versus hostile-combat escalation; live family runs revalidate interaction and feel rather than replacing those tests.
Earlier natural R-008 reports retain their exact focused dispatch, local-handoff, and return provenance; this family does not retroactively promote them.
current_uncertainty: No fresh bound family run yet connects a player-created exposed or occluded fire signal to the complete production-owned hostile and camp lifecycle with claim-scoped mixed-outcome evidence.
